name: Infleqtion, Inc.

profile.description: Infleqtion builds neutral-atom quantum computers, quantum sensors (optical clocks, RF receivers, inertial sensors) and software for governments, enterprises and research institutions. Founded in 2007 as ColdQuanta out of the University of Colorado Boulder, it listed on the NYSE in February 2026 via a merger with Churchill Capital Corp X. Q2 2026 revenue was restated to $13.5M (+157% YoY) from an originally reported $12.6M, and full-year 2026 guidance was raised to about $45.1M; the GAAP operating loss was $30.6M. On September 24, 2026 the company reported 30 entangled logical qubits on its Sqale system, with a roadmap to 100 logical qubits by 2028. It holds roughly $582M of cash and investments with no debt. Market cap approximately $2.0B at $8.88.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Infleqtion evolved from ColdQuanta's cold-atom components into full quantum computers and commercial sensors, and on September 24, 2026 reported 30 entangled logical qubits from 80 physical qubits on Sqale, hitting its 2026 target [3][1]. AI Deployment (1/2): It works with NVIDIA on CUDA-Q materials-science applications (management cites ~6x accuracy improvement), NVQLink integration, and NVIDIA's Ising AI models for calibration and decoding, but no quantified AI revenue or savings are reported [3]. Market Share (1/2): It is the first publicly listed neutral-atom quantum company and an early leader in quantum sensing, but private rivals compete in neutral atoms and share data is not disclosed [2]. Pipeline (2/2): The roadmap is explicit — 100 logical qubits by 2028, FY2026 revenue guidance of ~$45.1M, and a $100M CHIPS Act letter of intent [1][4]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D is about 102% of TTM revenue, top-quartile for the sector [5].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Infleqtion's purpose of commercializing quantum technology across computing and sensing is clear and rooted in 19 years of atomic-physics research, but it is not yet distinctive from other quantum companies or validated by long execution [3][2]. Community Impact (0/2): No company foundation or quantified community program was found. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): Insiders have been net sellers since listing — CTO Pranav Gokhale sold 120,000 shares at $17.73 in June 2026, director-linked entities of David Singer sold about 1.98M shares at ~$15.29-$15.98 in May 2026, director Kristina Johnson sold 50,000 shares, and Maverick Capital entities sold in August 2026 after one small purchase [6].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored (Growth, 8 available weight units): D/E of 2.5% scores 1.0 and revenue growth of 156.5% YoY scores 1.0 [5][7]. Every profitability metric scores 0: ROE of -38.2% (2x), profit margin of -167.8%, a negative forward P/E (-37.0), and a negative forward PEG (-0.10, 2x) since forward earnings are negative [5][7]. The 5yr revenue CAGR is excluded because pre-merger history in data providers reflects the SPAC shell. Weighted sum 2.0/8 = 2.5, rounding up to 3. Liquidity clears the floor easily (~8.1M shares/day x $8.88).

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9 — PROTECTED): Infleqtion sells physical quantum hardware — atomic clocks, RF receivers, inertial sensors and neutral-atom computers — that AI cannot replace; AI is instead used to calibrate and decode its machines via NVIDIA's Ising models and NVQLink, and the company positions quantum sensing for AI data centers [3]. Some quantum-computing use cases (optimization, simulation) could be partly addressed by improving classical AI, which keeps it out of the top tier. AI Opportunity (0/1): No quantified AI-related revenue is disclosed [1].

infinite_game.summary: Sinek would recognize a long-horizon scientific endeavor: Infleqtion spent nearly two decades on atomic physics before reaching meaningful revenue, and its roadmap is framed in multi-year logical-qubit milestones. But a SPAC listing, rapid insider selling and a revenue restatement within its first public year suggest the pressures of the finite market game are already shaping behavior.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Making quantum physics practically useful in both sensing and computing is a genuine, idealistic cause that has shaped the company since its 2007 university founding [3][2]. It has not yet been tested through a full commercial cycle or leadership transition at scale.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership is coherent — CEO Matthew Kinsella was Infleqtion's first investor in 2018 and joined full-time in April 2024, and CTO Pranav Gokhale frames progress as hardware-software co-design [3]. No retention data was found, and the Q2 revenue restatement over two government contracts is a minor control blemish [1].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Company messaging emphasizes being 'first' — first public neutral-atom company, first logical-qubit materials application — rather than learning from rivals; no evidence of framing competitors as worthy rivals was found [3][2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The shift from ColdQuanta's component business to integrated quantum computers and sensors, and the rebrand to Infleqtion, show meaningful adaptation [2]. It has not yet abandoned a profitable business in service of its cause.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): The company kept investing through years of losses — R&D still exceeds revenue — and committed publicly to 30 logical qubits in 2026, which it delivered [5][3]. The choice of a SPAC route and heavy insider selling soon after listing cut against a long-term signal [6].

investment_thesis: Infleqtion is executing on both revenue and technology: Q2 2026 revenue rose 157% (restated) to $13.5M, FY2026 guidance was lifted to ~$45.1M, it delivered 30 logical qubits in September 2026 on schedule, and it has a $100M CHIPS Act LOI [1][4][3]. With about $582M of cash and investments and no debt, it is funded for several years, and its sensing products (optical clocks, RF receivers) give it nearer-term commercial revenue than pure quantum-computing peers, alongside NVIDIA ecosystem integration [1][3].
thesis_continued: The bear case is valuation and execution: at ~$2.0B market cap the stock trades near 90x TTM sales with negative operating margins, a GAAP operating loss of $30.6M in Q2 versus $10.1M a year earlier, and stock compensation near 92% of revenue [5][1]. The Q2 revenue restatement, net insider selling by the CTO and directors, and a share price that has fallen from the high teens to $8.88 point to fragile sentiment [6][7]. Q2 operating cash flow was also flattered by a $27.4M payroll-tax timing benefit due to reverse in Q3 [1].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results confirming the ~$45.1M FY2026 revenue guidance after the Q2 restatement
Conversion of the $100M CHIPS Act letter of intent into a definitive award
Progress toward 100 logical qubits by 2028 on the Sqale platform
New government and data-center quantum-sensing contracts (optical clocks, RF receivers) and deeper NVIDIA NVQLink integration
key_risks: Cash burn from GAAP operating losses (~$30.6M per quarter) eroding the ~$582M cash balance and forcing dilution
Further revenue-recognition issues on government contracts after the Q2 2026 restatement
Continued insider and early-investor selling following the SPAC lock-up
Competition from private neutral-atom players and superconducting/trapped-ion rivals for logical-qubit leadership
